feature1.prompt: Auto-reloader should pass -X options (for cpython implementation). On Windows OS, when running 'python -X utf8 manage.py runserver', the auto-reloader must include the '-X' options (for example, '-Xutf8' or '-Xa=b') in the command invoked to relaunch the process. The implementation should detect if the interpreter is CPython and then correctly append these options to the argument list. This change is crucial to ensure that when Django starts the server—both in reloading and non-reloading modes—the specified '-X' options are honored.
feature1.hint_texts: Modify the Django auto-reloader by updating the get_child_arguments function in django/utils/autoreload.py. Check if sys.implementation.name is 'cpython' and, if so, extend the arguments list with '-X' options derived from sys._xoptions. Handle both boolean and key-value cases properly. Start by finding the existing argument list construction and insert the new logic right after the warnoptions processing.
feature1.entrypoint: File: django/utils/autoreload.py; Function: get_child_arguments; Insert a conditional block (around line 220) that, upon detecting a CPython environment, iterates over sys._xoptions and appends each option formatted as '-X{key}' (if the value is True) or '-X{key}={value}' (otherwise) to the arguments list.

tests.PASS_TO_PASS: Manual/script based tests verifying get_child_arguments behavior with '-X' options.

feature2.prompt: Auto-reloader should pass -X options (for cpython implementation). On Windows OS, commands like 'python -X utf8 manage.py runserver' or 'python -X utf8 manage.py runserver --noreload' must cause the auto-reloader to propagate the specified '-X' options to the child process. The system should reliably pass these options so that the intended runtime features, such as UTF-8 encoding, are activated. This behavior must hold in various scenarios, ensuring that the child process receives the complete and correctly formatted set of command-line arguments.
feature2.hint_texts: Enhance the automated tests in tests/utils_tests/test_autoreload.py to verify the new '-X' option functionality. Update existing test functions by adding mock patches for sys._xoptions and add a dedicated test (test_xoptions) that asserts the proper formation of the arguments list including the '-X' options. Ensure that the tests cover different scenarios, such as modules with or without __spec__ and various combinations of sys._xoptions values.
feature2.entrypoint: File: tests/utils_tests/test_autoreload.py; Update several test functions to include mock.patch entries for sys._xoptions and add a new test function named test_xoptions to check that get_child_arguments returns a list with the correctly formatted '-X' options.

collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Feature1 must correctly implement the '-X' option logic, ensuring that the argument list is built as expected. Feature2 then verifies this behavior through a comprehensive suite of automated tests. Both sides must coordinate so that any changes in the formatting or processing of sys._xoptions are reflected in the tests.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers working on the core implementation (Feature1) and those writing tests (Feature2) should sync frequently. Any modifications to sys._xoptions handling or get_child_arguments should be communicated immediately to ensure that the test suite remains in sync with the implementation.
